title: Ultra-light axion constraints from Planck and ACT: the role of nonlinear modelling (Gaughan, Green, Moss)
efc_relevance: MCMC analysis with Planck 2018 + ACT DR6 + DESI DR2 BAO of ultra-light axions in the mass range 10^-25 ≤ m/eV ≤ 10^-23. Shows that naive nonlinear modelling of non-cold matter produces an artificial preference for a subdominant ULA-DM component at m ≈ 10^-24 eV via a lensing-like enhancement of the CMB power spectrum — i.e. previously-claimed ULA detections are a modelling artefact. Tightens framework:FuzzyDM-Hu2000 by removing the spurious m ≈ 10^-24 eV preference and forces EFC discriminators against fuzzy-DM to be re-baselined against the corrected, weaker preference.
ledger_action: Add to External Research Ledger under cluster alternative-dark-matter; update framework:FuzzyDM-Hu2000 row to note the nonlinear-modelling caveat (no genuine m ≈ 10^-24 eV preference once nonlinear sector is treated correctly); cross-reference arXiv:2605.11600 (SPARC soliton+NFW) so the galactic-scale and CMB-scale ULA constraints share a single framework row.
